title: Kilt Quilt
statementMd:
An image set to be painted onto a tartan canvas consists of n𝑛 rows of m𝑚 pixels with each colour represented as a lowercase letter of the alphabet.

You are going to paint the image using long brush strokes that cover either a whole row of m𝑚 pixels, or a whole column of n pixels. Each brush stroke overwrites any pixels that were previously there. You must cover the whole canvas with brush strokes.

Is it possible to do so? If so, output a sequence of instructions of the form `x=[1-m] [a-z]` or `y=[1-n] [a-z]`. If there are multiple sequences, output any of the shortest possible lists of instructions.

![image](https://espresso.codeforces.com/26cffd146178d85441095ce3947c846af074134d.png)Illustration of Sample Input 2.

## Input

- The first line of input contains n and m (1≤n,m≤200)
- The next n lines of input contain a string of m lowercase characters in `a-z`, each representing a colour.

## Output

On the first line, output the minimum number of instructions needed. If no sequence of instructions covers the canvas, output `impossible` and exit.

On each of the next lines, output one instruction to follow in order. For example, "`x=5 z`", and "`y=100 b`" are both valid instructions.

samples.output:
5
y=1 a
y=2 a
y=3 a
y=4 a
x=5 b

6
x=1 l
y=2 d
x=2 a
x=3 a
y=4 b
x=4 q
